sections.executive_summary:
Maryland calls this service **Community Living – Group Home (CL–GH)**. It is a provider-owned or provider-operated home for adults (18+) with intellectual and developmental disabilities, funded through the **Community Pathways Waiver (CPW)** and run by the Maryland Department of Health's **Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA)** [S8]. Since **October 6, 2025** the Family Supports and Community Supports waivers have been merged into the CPW. It is now DDA's only waiver [S1]. To operate, you need three things: **DDA approval** as a qualified provider, a **license issued under COMAR 10.22.02**, with the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) acting as DDA's licensing and survey agent, and a **Medicaid (MA) number for each licensed site** [S8][S26][S30].

**The rate structure is by home size, not by support level.** LTSSMaryland pays W5600 per person per day. The rate depends on how many people live in the home (1–8), whether overnight supervision is provided, and whether the person lives in a geographic-differential county [S3][S9]. Individual intensity is funded separately through **dedicated 1:1 or 2:1 hours** (W1999/W2000) and Nursing Support Services (W5804) [S3][S8]. The October 1, 2026 rate chart pays **$403.30/day** in a 4-person home with overnight supervision, or $443.63 in Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery and Prince George's counties [S3][S9]. The FY 2027 budget includes a **2% provider rate cut**, but DDA says rates **stay at June 30, 2026 levels until CMS approves the waiver amendment**. CMS asked for more information on September 25, 2026 [S5][S6].

**The binding constraints are the size limit and the entry bar.** New CL–GH homes may serve **no more than four participants per residence** unless DDA approved more beforehand, and each person gets a private bedroom unless they choose to share [S8]. Applicants must show **at least five years of demonstrated DD residential experience**, a governing body that includes a person with a developmental disability and a family member, a business plan, a program service plan and a DDA-approved quality assurance plan [S8][S17][S20]. There is **no published application window**: DDA takes applications by email on a rolling basis [S13]. On the Medicaid side, enrollment was on hold during the move from ePREP to the new **MPRIME** system, which went live **October 13, 2026** [S31][S32].

**Demand is steady.** 6,849 people received DDA residential services in FY2025, and CL–GH was the largest single DDA service at 32% of $3.3 billion in spending. The community-services waiting list was 3,465 on June 30, 2025 [S34]. **The economics are thin, and vacancies cost more than they look.** DDA pays the W5600 rate for the number of people actually living in the home [S62], so when one of four residents leaves, the other three drop to the 3-person rate ($355.23) and the home loses about 34% of its W5600 revenue, not 25% [S3]. The model prices that in with an occupancy-blended rate ($387.28 effective at 90% occupancy for a 4-person home). On that basis, with paid training time, conservative nursing revenue and the 2027 FAMLI contribution included, a single 4-person Baltimore-area home nets about **+$1,919/month** at 90% occupancy (break-even about 86–87%). Two homes net about **+$1,976**, a 4-person home in a differential county about **+$2,574**, and a home with two residents authorized for 1:1 dedicated hours about **+$6,849**. A **3-person home nets about +$1,413** and is the most vacancy-resistant option, because a vacancy moves the remaining two residents to the higher 2-person rate ($478.09); it still roughly breaks even at 80% occupancy, where every 4-person configuration loses money. All results are sensitive to DSP wages, paid time off and vacancies (Section 8).
sections.service_model:
### What the service is
CL–GH builds and maintains skills in daily living, household tasks, communication, safety, self-care and community participation, using formal teaching methods in a community residential setting [S8]. The daily rate includes **transportation** to, from and within the service, **delegated nursing tasks** and **personal care assistance** based on assessed need. Delegated medication tasks must be done by staff certified as **Medication Technicians by the Maryland Board of Nursing** [S8].

### Who qualifies
Participants must be adults on the CPW and preauthorized by DDA. DDA must find that the person has critical support needs that other residential or in-home services cannot meet, and that the group home is the most integrated, cost-effective option. The person must also meet one of the listed criteria, such as homelessness, imminent risk at home, caregiver incapacity, abuse or neglect risk, or discharge from a hospital, institution or incarceration with no other setting [S8].

### Setting requirements
- The home must be **owned or operated by the provider** [S8].
- **No more than four participants per residence** unless previously approved by DDA [S8]. The rate chart still lists sizes up to 8, which apply to homes DDA approved earlier [S3].
- A **private single bedroom** for each person unless two people choose to share [S8].
- Full compliance with the federal **HCBS settings rule** for provider-owned or controlled settings: a lease or equivalent, lockable doors, choice of roommate, freedom to furnish, access to food and visitors at any time [S52]. DDA's new-site checklist flags sites close to the provider's other sites, sites in gated communities and 'one-stop-shop' settings for heightened scrutiny [S60].
- Services are provided at least 6 hours a day or overnight. A **residential retainer fee** covers up to 18 days per resident per calendar year for hospitalization, behavioral respite or family visits [S8]. On retainer days the absent resident still counts toward the home size for billing [S62].

### Money that is not in the rate
Medicaid does **not** pay room and board. The provider collects room and board, and any assessed contribution to the cost of care, directly from the participant [S8][S9]. Most residents rely on SSI, which is $994/month for an individual in 2026 [S51].

### Regulatory framework
- **COMAR 10.22.02**: licensing, governing body, program service plan, policies, staffing, health and safety, records and quality assurance [S16][S17][S20][S21][S22].
- **COMAR 10.22.08**: community residential services. Group homes and alternative living units (ALUs) are residential models, and staffing levels follow each person's plan [S24][S25].
- **Community Pathways Waiver, Appendix C (service definition) and Appendix I (rates)** [S8][S9].
- **42 CFR §441.301(c)(4)**: HCBS settings rule [S52].
- A separate service, **Community Living – Enhanced Supports**, covers people with intensive needs at higher rates (e.g., $569.34/day in a 4-person home) under its own license category [S3][S14]. Children's residential services need COMAR 14.31 compliance as well [S16].
sections.licensing_pathway:
Maryland has **three linked approvals**. DDA approves you as a qualified provider. A COMAR 10.22.02 license is then issued, with OHCQ as DDA's licensing and survey agent. Finally, Medicaid enrolls each licensed site. The steps below follow DDA's current instructions and forms.

### Step 1 — Form the right entity
COMAR requires the licensee to be **properly organized as a Maryland corporation** (or a registered foreign corporation) [S17]. The 2026 waiver text says 'Maryland business entity' [S8], but archived OHCQ guidance states that **DDA does not accept LLCs** because they lack a governing body [S28]. Form a stock or nonstock corporation with SDAT to be safe. Articles cost $100 plus a $20 organization and capitalization fee; nonstock 501(c)(3) corporations pay $50 more [S43]. Get an EIN [S55] and a Type 2 NPI [S56]. Since **October 13, 2026**, Medicaid will not accept an MPRIME application without an SDAT ID in good standing [S31].

### Step 2 — Build a compliant governing body
The governing body must include **at least one person with a developmental disability, one family member of such a person, and one person with DD experience**. At least 75% of members must live in Maryland or within 100 miles of the in-state administrative office. **Employees and their immediate family may not be voting members**, and **board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee** [S20]. The last rule rules out the common plan of an owner buying the house and leasing it to the agency.

### Step 3 — Prepare the application package
Use the **DDA Provider Application (form rev. 9.19.25)** and its instructions (rev. 09-25-2025) [S13][S14]. Check 'Adult Community Living Group Home Services' under Licensed Services [S14]. Required items include:
- Resumes of the CEO/Director and all managers, showing **at least 5 years of relevant DD experience** [S14][S8], and three professional references [S14].
- A **Program Service Plan** (COMAR 10.22.02.09), a **Quality Assurance Plan**, a **business plan**, and a **first-year budget plus a second-year projection** [S14][S17].
- A **bank letter dated within 30 days** showing a line of credit, loan or available funds, because 'payment for services… may not be received for up to 180 days from the date of service initiation' [S14].
- General liability insurance (a quote is acceptable for initial applicants), auto insurance, workers' compensation and unemployment insurance [S14].
- Governing Body form, Staff Training form, Staff Criminal History form, Policies & Procedures form, List of Licensed Site Locations, the signed **Provider Agreement to Conditions of Participation** and the mandatory checklist [S13][S15][S58].
- Prior licensing reports from the past 10 years for any associated entity [S17].

### Step 4 — Background checks before you submit
Request **CJIS fingerprint checks** for the applicant and first-line managers **at least two weeks before** you submit. Use DDA Agency Authorization #1500001484 and ORI MD003105Y, and check 'Government Licensing or Certification'. If DDA headquarters has not received the results **within 30 days of receiving the application, the application will not be approved** [S13]. Child Protective Services clearances are needed only if you will serve children [S13].

### Step 5 — Submit (no application window)
Email the package to **providerapplications.dda@maryland.gov**, with your DDA Regional Office in the subject line. Hard copies are not accepted [S13]. DDA publishes no application window or cohort. On the Medicaid side, new-enrollment applications were on hold from July 1 (high/moderate-risk types) or August 1 (limited-risk types) 2026 until MPRIME launched on October 13, 2026 [S31].

### Step 6 — DDA decision and the OHCQ phase
After approval, an initial applicant seeking a licensed service is told to **contact OHCQ for the next phase of licensing** [S29]. If DDA approves the application, **policies and procedures must be submitted to OHCQ within 30 days** [S14]. Under COMAR the Director may approve unconditionally, approve with conditions, deny, or ask for more information [S17]. Archived OHCQ guidance describes a Letter of Interest, a quarterly **Applicant Interest Session**, and a document list that includes P&Ps, business plan, program plan, QA template and table of organization [S27][S28]. Confirm the current process with OHCQ's DD team. The published number, 410-402-8100 (toll-free 877-402-8220), is OHCQ's Developmental Disabilities main/complaint line; ask for the DD licensing team [S26]. There is no state license fee schedule for DDA licenses in COMAR 10.22.02 [S17].

### Step 7 — Site approval and survey
Each home must meet local zoning (subject to the exception in Health-General §7-603), building and life-safety codes, keep **water at or below 110°F**, and have smoke detectors, working fire extinguishers and a written evacuation plan [S22]. Request site approval with the **DDA Addendum for Licensed Services and Sites** (MDH Form DD.ADD.1.0, which includes a settings-rule attestation) [S59]. The DDA regional office runs a **New Site Visit checklist** [S60]. After DDA approves a new site, OHCQ surveys it, **generally within 4–6 weeks** for existing licensees [S26]. Any later new site, closure or relocation needs DDA approval **at least 30 days in advance** [S18]. The license states your licensed capacity [S19].

### Step 8 — Medicaid enrollment per site
Each licensed site needs its own **'DDA Licensed Site MA' number** (PT 90 DDA addendum) [S30]. MPRIME replaced ePREP on October 13, 2026 [S31][S32]. Providers whose complete applications are in MPRIME by December 31, 2026 get backdated enrollment to the start of the application hold or the license date, whichever is later [S31]. DDA says DDA-approved providers will register in MPRIME in 2027 and that it will issue guidance [S6]. The federal enrollment application fee is $750 in CY2026 [S33]. Confirm in MPRIME whether it applies to PT 90 DDA.

### Step 9 — Renewal
File renewals at least 60 days before expiration. The renewal approval is good for **up to 3 years** [S8][S17].
sections.reimbursement:
### How the money flows
Community Pathways is a 1915(c) waiver. DDA authorizes services in each person's **Person-Centered Plan (PCP)**, and providers bill **fee-for-service in LTSSMaryland**. There is no managed care layer [S9][S34]. Rates come from the **Brick Method**: a BLS direct-support wage plus Employment Related Expenses, Program Support, Training and Transportation components and a 12% G&A component [S9]. DDA may fund rates at a percentage of the fully loaded Brick, depending on budget [S9]. DDA's FY2024 Brick workbook builds CL–GH rates on BLS 21-1093 (Social and Human Service Assistants) at the median, with **43.14 staff-hours per day for a 4-person home with overnight supervision** and **28.5 for a 3-person home** [S10]. The model in Section 8 uses those funded hours.

### Current CL–GH rates (W5600, per person per day)
| Residents in home | With overnight supervision | Differential | Without overnight | Differential |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | $737.16 | $810.88 | $438.02 | $481.82 |
| 2 | $478.09 | $525.89 | $328.52 | $361.37 |
| 3 | $355.23 | $390.75 | $255.51 | $281.06 |
| 4 | $403.30 | $443.63 | $328.52 | $361.37 |

Source: FY2027 LTSSMaryland Rate Chart from October 1, 2026 (identical to the October 6, 2025 rates) [S2][S3][S1]. Sizes 5–8 appear in Appendix A but are limited to homes DDA approved earlier [S8]. The 4-person rate is **higher** than the 3-person rate because the Brick model funds a second staff for most of the day in a 4-person home [S10].

**The rate follows the actual census, not the licensed capacity.** Providers must enter the 'Number of People Authorized' on each residential claim, defined as everyone living in the home with active waiver enrollment who is present that day or on a retainer day (max 18 days per year) [S62]. If a 4-person home has one vacancy, the remaining three residents are billed at the 3-person rate ($403.30 → $355.23). If a 3-person home has one vacancy, the remaining two are billed at the 2-person rate ($355.23 → $478.09) [S3]. DDA's Residential Rate Discrepancy reports correct claims billed at the wrong size [S62].

### Add-on revenue
- **Dedicated hours** (W1999 1:1 = $11.44 per 15 min; W2000 2:1 = $22.88), authorized for a documented behavioral or nursing need, or for up to 6 months for people new to services while a behavior plan is developed [S3][S8]. Shared use of dedicated hours is limited to residents who are retired, transitioning between day services, recovering from a health condition, or receiving few day-service hours: fewer than 40 hours in the current text, lowered to fewer than 30 hours in Amendment #4, which is pending CMS approval [S64][S6]. Dedicated hours are billed for one participant only [S6][S8].
- **Nursing Support Services** (W5804 = $30.77 per 15 min), authorized from the Health Risk Screening Tool [S3][S8]. A 2018 DDA webinar said nursing is not included in the residential rate [S29]. The 2026 CL–GH definition, however, says the service **includes** Nursing Support Services based on assessed need, and that **additional standalone** NSS hours can be authorized by the Regional Office after a change in health status or a hospital/nursing-facility discharge [S8]. Do not count on standalone NSS for every resident; the model assumes it for one resident in four.
- **Retainer fee** (W5604) for up to 18 absence days per year [S8]. The CL Rates tab shows no separate retainer amount; retainer days keep the absent resident counted toward the home-size rate [S62][S3]. **Trial experience** (W5602) $423.05/day [S3].
- **Room and board** from the resident, outside Medicaid [S8].

### Geographic differential
Residents of Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery and Prince George's counties generate the differential rate. It is about 10% above standard and is based on Washington DC-metro BLS wages [S9][S54].

### Rate outlook
DDA providers received at least 3% every year from FY2016 to FY2025. **FY2026 and FY2027 have 0% increases** [S34]. The FY2027 budget adds a **2% reduction** for provider-managed services and caps support-service funding at 102% of the fully loaded rate [S6][S7]. DDA published the reduced rates (e.g., $395.23 for 4 with overnight) [S4], but it states that **rates remain at June 30, 2026 levels until CMS approves the amendment** [S5]. The October 1, 2026 chart still shows the higher rates [S3]. Budget for both.
sections.demand:
### Who is waiting and who is served
- DDA served **19,158** people across its waivers in FY2025 (20,376 in community services) [S34]. DDA cites about 19,000 Marylanders served [S6].
- **6,849 participants received residential services** in FY2025. That was the first year residential outnumbered meaningful-day participants (5,984). DDA estimates **$239,616 per residential participant** in FY2027 [S34].
- The **community-services waiting list was 3,465** on June 30, 2025: 2 in crisis resolution, 202 in crisis prevention and 3,261 current requests. It was 5,637 in FY2018 [S34]. The FY2027 allowance funds **994 new participants** [S34].
- CL–GH accounted for **32% of FY2025 DDA spending**, and dedicated hours for another 18% [S34].

### How referrals actually reach you
- Every participant has a **Coordinator of Community Services (CCS)**, the targeted case manager who builds the PCP and helps choose providers [S34]. Building relationships with CCS agencies in your region is the main business-development task.
- DDA's **four Regional Offices** (Central, Eastern Shore, Southern, Western) oversee services and provider relations. Southern Maryland covers Calvert, Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's and St. Mary's [S35].
- DDA's public 'Find a Provider' directory is at maryland.providersearch.com [S12].
- Eligibility for CL–GH is need-based (crisis, caregiver loss, institutional discharge and similar) [S8]. Expect referrals to involve urgent placements and people coming out of hospitals or other settings.

### Practical demand signal
With a residential census of about 6,849 and a 4-person cap on new homes [S34][S8], new capacity comes in small units. Competition is for staff and for CCS trust more than for raw demand. No public source gives vacancy rates or waitlists by county.
sections.operations:
### Staffing rules
Maryland sets **no fixed staff ratio** for group homes. The licensee must analyze each person's needs and run a staffing plan that meets the health, safety and services in each plan [S21][S25]. The provider must also ensure services are available **24/7 at each licensed site, with back-up and emergency support** [S8]. The model staffs at the hours DDA's rate funds: **43.14 staff-hours per day for a 4-person home with overnight supervision** [S10], plus 1.6% for paid training time, the training factor in DDA's own FY2025 cost analysis (27.3 hours per FTE per year) [S11].

### Staff qualifications and training
- Age 18+, **First Aid and CPR with an in-person skills session**, background checks, a valid driver's license if driving, and insured vehicles [S8].
- Before independent duties: training to do the job, DDA-approved training for the people served (seizures, behavior change, managing disruptive behavior, **medication administration**, aging), and OSHA blood-borne pathogens [S21].
- **Within 3 months of hire**: community integration, person-centered planning, characteristics of people served, first aid/CPR, rights, communicable diseases, supporting choice and communication skills [S21].
- **Medication Technician certification** (Maryland Board of Nursing) for any unlicensed staff paid to give medication or treatments [S8]. Medications must follow DDA's medication curriculum, be packaged in unit doses, and use pharmacy-generated MARs [S22].
- **Criminal history checks** before hire for everyone with direct contact (Health-General §19-1901 et seq.) [S21][S13]. Screen against the OIG exclusion list [S57][S13].
- No relatives, legal guardians or legally responsible persons may be paid to provide CL–GH [S8].

### Required policies and plans
Policies must meet COMAR 10.22.02.10 and go to OHCQ within 30 days of DDA approval [S14]. You also need a Program Service Plan (reviewed by the governing body at least every 3 years), a DDA-approved QA plan and written job descriptions [S14][S21].

### Incidents and inspections
Licensees are open to **announced and unannounced inspections**. Report incidents under DDA's Policy on Reportable Incidents and Investigations. OHCQ starts Priority 1 (immediate jeopardy) investigations within 2 working days, and **plans of correction are due within 10 working days** of receiving deficiencies [S23].

### Systems
- **LTSSMaryland** for PCP service authorizations and billing [S9][S12].
- **EVV is required for Personal Supports and Respite, not for CL–GH** [S9].
- An EHR/eMAR is an operator choice. DDA mandates no vendor.

### Room-and-board administration
Set a written room-and-board agreement with each resident. The settings rule requires a lease or equivalent agreement [S52]. Collect it separately from Medicaid billing [S8].
sections.market_conditions:
### Supply
DLS counted **338 DDA providers** billing in LTSSMaryland by FY2025 across all services [S34]. DDA's 2024 flyer listed 254 DDA-approved and licensed providers [S35]. Neither figure is a count of group-home operators. The 4-person cap since the settings-rule transition means new entrants add small homes, and DDA scrutinizes clustering [S8][S60].

### Wages (BLS OEWS, May 2025)
| Role | Maryland | Baltimore MSA | DC MSA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Social & human service assistants (21-1093), 25th pct | $20.30 | $19.57 | $20.74 |
| 21-1093 median | $22.70 | $23.28 | $23.26 |
| Home health & personal care aides (31-1120), mean | $18.99 | $18.73 | $18.80 |
| Registered nurses (29-1141), mean | $47.60 | $47.64 | $50.28 |
| Social & community service managers (11-9151), median | $42.04 | $40.75 | $48.67 |

Sources: [S36][S37][S38]. The state minimum wage is **$15.00**. Montgomery County's is **$18.00** for employers with 51+ workers, **$16.50** for 11–50 workers (certain nonprofits and Medicaid-funded home care providers also pay the mid-size rate regardless of size) and **$15.95** for 10 or fewer. Howard County's is **$16.00** and Prince George's County's is **$15.30** (July 1, 2026) [S39]. The modeled DSP wages ($19.57 and $20.74) are above every local minimum. DDA's own FY2025 general-ledger analysis grouped residential services under a uniform DSP wage, and it notes that some GL wages differ materially from BLS [S11].

### Housing costs
HUD FY2027 4-bedroom Small Area FMRs run from **$1,890 (Hagerstown)** to **$2,750 (Parkville), $3,100 (Glen Burnie), $3,590 (Silver Spring) and $4,050 (Upper Marlboro)** [S45][S46][S47][S48][S49]. A 4-resident home needs four private bedrooms, and usually space for staff too [S8]. The model therefore uses $3,400 (Baltimore metro) and $4,300 (Prince George's/Montgomery), both labeled operator estimates.

### Trends
- **No rate increase in FY2026 or FY2027**, a pending 2% cut, and new limits on shared dedicated hours [S34][S6].
- DDA's cost growth (+$920M in general funds and 144% over five years) is driving cost containment [S6].
- Waiver consolidation (Oct 2025) and the MPRIME enrollment system (Oct 2026) are both changing administration [S1][S31].
sections.financial_narrative:
### How the pro forma is built
**Revenue per occupied bed** has three parts:
- The W5600 daily rate × 30.42 days, entered as an **occupancy-blended effective rate** (explained below) [S3][S62].
- Nursing Support Services at 8 units a month ($30.77/unit) for **one resident in four** [S3]. This is a conservative operator estimate: the 2026 service definition includes NSS in the group-home service and authorizes extra standalone hours case by case [S8].
- Room and board of $850/month from the resident. This is an operator estimate below the $994 SSI benefit [S8][S51].

Base revenue is **$12,693 per occupied resident-month** in the standard 4-person home.

### Why the W5600 rate is blended
DDA pays the W5600 rate for the **number of people actually living in the home** (present, or on a retainer day) on each date of service [S62]. A vacancy therefore re-prices every remaining resident:
- **4-person home:** full house $403.30 each; with one empty bed the other three are billed $355.23 each [S3]. One vacancy cuts daily W5600 revenue from $1,613.20 to $1,065.69 (−34%).
- **3-person home:** full house $355.23 each; with one empty bed the other two are billed the 2-person rate of $478.09 [S3]. Daily revenue falls only from $1,065.69 to $956.18 (−10%).

The shared P&L model bills one rate × billable census, so the rate entered is the **expected rate per billable resident-day** at the default 90% occupancy. It assumes at most one bed is empty at a time (vacancies are filled one at a time):
- Share of days with one empty bed = (1 − occupancy) × capacity = 0.10 × 4 = **40%** for a 4-bed home (0.10 × 3 = 30% for a 3-bed home).
- Blended rate = (capacity × full-house share × full rate + (capacity − 1) × vacancy share × smaller-home rate) ÷ (capacity × occupancy).
- 4-person standard: (4 × 0.6 × $403.30 + 3 × 0.4 × $355.23) ÷ 3.6 = **$387.28**. Differential: $443.63/$390.75 → **$426.00**. At the proposed −2% rates: $395.23/$348.12 → **$379.53**.
- 3-person standard: (3 × 0.7 × $355.23 + 2 × 0.3 × $478.09) ÷ 2.7 = **$382.53**, higher than the 3-person rate itself.

The blended rate changes with occupancy: at 80% it is $367.25 for a 4-person home and $416.66 for a 3-person home; at 97% it is $398.84 and $362.83. The P&L keeps the 90% figure in every scenario, so its 80% column **understates** the 4-person loss and overstates the 3-person loss. The table shows both.

**Staffing is fixed coverage tied to DDA's funded hours**, because Maryland sets no ratio [S21][S25]:
- **4-person home:** 1,333 paid DSP hours a month: 1,312 Brick coverage hours (43.14/day) [S10] × 1.016 for paid required training time, DDA's own training factor for Community Living (27.3 hrs per FTE per year) [S11]. Wage **$19.57**, the BLS Baltimore MSA 25th percentile for 21-1093 [S37]; DDA's Brick uses the same occupation at the median and funds $19.53/hr [S10]. Program director at 20 hrs/week ($40.75, 11-9151 median). RN delegating nurse at 6 fixed hours plus 0.5 hour per resident for the conditional NSS ($47.64) [S37].
- **3-person home:** 881 DSP hours (28.5/day × 1.016) [S10][S11].
- **Two homes:** 2,666 DSP hours, a full-time director and a 20 hr/week billing coordinator ($26.90) [S36].
- **Differential county:** DC-metro wages ($20.74 DSP, $48.67 director, $50.28 RN) [S38], above every local minimum wage [S39].
- **Dedicated-hours case:** two of four residents get 4 hrs/day of 1:1 (W1999 $11.44/15 min), staffed hour for hour plus the training factor [S3][S11].

**Payroll burden is 16.95%:** FICA 7.65%, plus FUTA, plus Maryland UI up to 2.6% on $8,500 (about 8.5% combined) [S42][S41], plus the **Maryland FAMLI employer contribution of 0.45%** on wages paid from January 1, 2027 (employers with 15+ employees) [S63]; workers' comp 4% (estimate); and sick leave and benefits 4% [S40].

**Operating costs:** rent is fixed per home (see Section 7). Food uses the USDA moderate plan at $366 per resident [S50]. The SDAT annual report is $300/yr for a stock corporation [S44]. Insurance, vehicle, software and other items are labeled operator estimates.

### Results at 90% default occupancy (the generator recomputes)
| Configuration | Revenue/mo | Net/mo at 90% | Net at 80% (P&L, 90% blended rate) | Net at 80% (rate re-priced for 80%) | Break-even occupancy (P&L / re-priced) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4-person group home, Baltimore metro, two residents with 1:1 dedicated hours | ≈ $55,716 | ≈ +$6,849 | ≈ +$1,429 | ≈ −$520 | ≈ 77% / 81% |
| 4-person group home, Prince George's/Montgomery (geographic differential rate) | ≈ $49,950 | ≈ +$2,574 | ≈ −$2,770 | ≈ −$4,914 | ≈ 85% / 87% |
| Two 4-person group homes, Baltimore metro (shared director) | ≈ $91,387 | ≈ +$1,976 | ≈ −$7,767 | ≈ −$11,666 | ≈ 88% / 89% |
| 4-person group home, Baltimore metro (standard rate) | ≈ $45,693 | ≈ +$1,919 | ≈ −$2,953 | ≈ −$4,903 | ≈ 86% / 87% |
| 3-person group home, Baltimore metro (standard rate) | ≈ $33,880 | ≈ +$1,413 | ≈ −$2,198 | ≈ +$294 | ≈ 86% / 77% |
| 4-person group home, Baltimore metro, at the proposed FY2027 rates (−2%) | ≈ $44,836 | ≈ +$1,061 | ≈ −$3,715 | ≈ −$5,626 | ≈ 88% / 88% |

Every configuration is profitable at 90%, but only narrowly; the margin on a single 4-person home is about 4% of revenue.

### What drives the result
1. **Vacancy.** In a 4-bed home one empty bed costs about 34% of W5600 revenue, so the single home needs about 87% occupancy once the rate step-down is priced in, and loses about $4,903/month at 80%. Billing the full 4-person rate on every occupied day would have shown +$3,673/month at 90%; the step-down costs about $1,750/month. The **3-person home** is the vacancy-resistant option: at 80% it still nets about +$294/month, and its re-priced break-even is about 77%.
2. **DSP wage.** At the Maryland 21-1093 **median of $22.70** instead of $19.57, the base home moves to about **−$2,961/month**. Every $1/hour on 1,333 hours costs about $1,560/month with burden.
3. **Paid time off.** The model pays only training time and statutory sick leave. DDA's own cost analysis uses a residential productivity factor of 1.15 (about 245 non-billable hours per FTE per year, including PTO and holidays) [S11]. If you offer PTO and holidays at that level (replacing the separate sick-leave allowance), the base home moves to about **−$1,002/month**, two homes to about −$3,791, the 3-person home to about −$474, and the dedicated-hours home to about +$3,419.
4. **Nursing revenue.** With no standalone NSS at all, the base home nets about +$1,798/month. If DDA authorizes 8 units for every resident, about +$2,283.
5. **Room and board.** With zero room-and-board income the base home loses about $1,141/month, because food and household costs then come out of the Medicaid rate.
6. **The pending 2% cut** lowers the base home to about **+$1,061/month** (break-even about 88%) [S4].
7. **Dedicated hours** are the strongest lever (+$6,849/month in the modeled case), but they depend on individual authorizations and the FY2027 limits on shared use [S6][S64].
8. **Scale.** A second home adds a full-time director and a billing coordinator, so at 90% two homes net about the same as one (+$1,976/month) and lose about $11,666/month at 80% once the rate step-down is priced in. Scale pays off only with high occupancy or dedicated-hours residents.

### Cash needs
DDA warns that payment may take **up to 180 days** after services start, and it wants a bank letter showing start-up funds [S14]. The P&L shows the modeled ramp-up deficit. Hold extra reserves in case that 180-day lag actually happens.
sections.risks:
### Rate and policy risk
- **The 2% cut is pending CMS approval** [S5][S6]. No rate increases are budgeted for FY2026–FY2027 [S34]. Model at the reduced rates (about +$1,061/month for the base home) before you commit.
- **Shared dedicated-hours rules** now limit when one authorized 1:1 staff can support several residents [S6][S8]. Revenue from dedicated hours depends on individual authorizations, which can change at each PCP review.
- **Cost-neutrality pressure** on the waiver led DDA to warn of possible emergency service cuts or freezes if the program falls out of federal compliance [S6].

### Cash-flow risk
- DDA itself warns of payment delays up to **180 days** [S14].
- Each site needs its own MA number, and MPRIME is brand new as of October 13, 2026 [S30][S31].
- Medicaid suspends providers who lose SDAT good standing or let a license lapse (license updates due by March 31, 2027) [S31].

### Operating risk
- **Vacancies** in a 4-bed home. A vacancy drops every remaining resident to the smaller-home rate (4 → 3 people: $403.30 → $355.23), so one empty bed costs about 34% of the home's W5600 revenue, not 25% [S62][S3]. The single 4-person home loses about $4,903/month at 80% occupancy (Section 8). Placements depend on DDA authorization and CCS referrals [S8].
- **Wages.** Montgomery County's $18.00 minimum and DC-metro competition raise labor costs. At the Maryland 21-1093 median ($22.70) the base home loses about $2,961 a month [S39][S36]. Offering PTO and holidays at DDA's 1.15 productivity factor turns the base home to about −$1,002 a month [S11].
- **Nursing revenue** is uncertain: the 2026 service definition includes Nursing Support Services within the group-home service and authorizes standalone hours case by case [S8]. The model assumes standalone NSS for only one resident in four.
- **New payroll costs:** Maryland FAMLI contributions start on wages paid from January 1, 2027 (0.45% employer share at 15+ employees) [S63].
- **Medication administration** requires CMT-certified staff and RN delegation. Losing the delegating nurse stops medication passes [S8].
- **Incidents and surveys.** POCs are due in 10 working days, and serious incidents can trigger investigations within 2 working days [S23].

### Structural and legal risk
- **Entity type:** COMAR requires a corporation [S17]. An LLC may be rejected [S28].
- **Related-party real estate:** board members and employees may not own property leased back to the licensee [S20].
- **Five-year experience requirement:** applicants without five years of DD residential experience will likely need an experienced leader or partner [S8].
- **Settings-rule scrutiny** of clustered or isolated sites [S60][S52].
- **Ending services** to a resident requires 90 days' written notice and the Director's approval [S17].
sections.recommendations:
1. **Confirm the entry bar first.** Make sure your leadership can document **5+ years of DD residential experience** [S8]. If it can't, recruit an experienced director or partner before spending on a house.
2. **Incorporate, don't form an LLC.** Form a Maryland stock or nonstock corporation with SDAT ($120+) [S43][S17]. Seat a compliant board that includes a person with a DD, a family member and a DD professional, with no employees as voting members [S20].
3. **Keep the real estate at arm's length.** Do not lease the home from board members or employees [S20]. Lease from an unrelated landlord, or put the property in a structure your attorney confirms meets COMAR 10.22.02.08C(9).
4. **Pick the home size for your vacancy risk.** A 3-person home is the lower-risk choice: a vacancy moves the other two residents to the 2-person rate ($478.09), so it nets about +$1,413/month at 90% and still about breaks even at 80% [S3][S62]. A 4-person home has more upside (about +$1,919 at 90%, +$6,693 at 97%), but one vacancy re-prices the other three to $355.23 and it loses about $4,903/month at 80%. Choose four bedrooms only if you have referrals lined up. Either way, choose an accessible house that is not near your other sites [S8][S60].
5. **Run fingerprints two weeks before you submit,** and email a complete package to providerapplications.dda@maryland.gov [S13]. Have P&Ps ready to send to OHCQ within 30 days of DDA approval [S14].
6. **Enroll in MPRIME as soon as you are eligible.** Get your SDAT ID in good standing first [S31].
7. **Build the census deliberately.** Meet the CCS agencies and your DDA Regional Office before opening [S35]. Ask about residents who qualify for dedicated hours or nursing support. In the modeled case dedicated hours more than triple the margin (+$6,849/month vs +$1,919) [S3][S8]. Ask DDA whether standalone nursing hours will be authorized; do not assume them for every resident [S8].
8. **Plan for 90%+ occupancy before adding a second home.** Once the rate step-down is priced in, a single 4-person home needs about 87% occupancy to break even. Two homes with a full-time director net only about +$1,976/month at 90%, so add the second home when the first is full and the director's time is already covered.
9. **Price your labor honestly.** Use your local wage. The DC metro and Montgomery County cost more [S38][S39]. Re-run the P&L at $22.70/hour (base home about −$2,961/month), with PTO and holidays if you offer them, and at the −2% rates [S36][S11][S4]. Register for Maryland FAMLI contributions, which start on wages paid from January 1, 2027 [S63].
10. **Fund the payment lag.** Hold the modeled ramp-up deficit plus a cushion for DDA's possible 180-day payment delay [S14].

occupancy.rationale: DDA publishes no group-home occupancy data. 90% is a planning assumption; 80% stress-tests a long vacancy. A vacancy costs more than its share of beds: DDA pays the rate for the number of people actually living in the home [S62], so in a 4-bed home one empty bed drops the other three from $403.30 to $355.23 a day and cuts W5600 revenue by about 34% (not 25%). In a 3-bed home a vacancy moves the other two to the 2-person rate ($478.09), which cushions the loss [S3]. The model folds this into an occupancy-blended W5600 rate (see Section 8). revenue_lines.notes: Effective per-resident rate at 90% occupancy, not a published rate. Published rates [S3]: $355.23 when all 3 beds are filled, $478.09 when 2 people live in the home. corrections_vs_previous: The old Maryland group-home research described group homes as serving 4–8 individuals. The current Community Living – Group Home standard allows no more than four participants per residence unless previously approved by DDA, with private bedrooms [S8].

The old research inferred a one-year 'provisional' first license. COMAR 10.22.02.02 has no provisional term: the Director may approve with conditions [S17], and the waiver standard makes renewals good for up to 3 years [S8].

The old research said the property owner and the agency can share an owner through separate LLCs. COMAR 10.22.02.08C(9) prohibits governing-body members and employees from owning property leased back to the licensee [S20].
Old materials and client templates used LLC entities. COMAR requires a Maryland corporation [S17], and archived OHCQ guidance states DDA does not accept LLCs [S28].
The old research said there was no overconcentration test. DDA's New Site Visit checklist flags a site near other sites the same organization operates for heightened scrutiny [S60].
The old research attributed licensing decisions to OHCQ's Director. Under COMAR the DDA Director issues and denies licenses, and OHCQ is DDA's licensing and survey agent [S17][S26].

The old DDA agency P&L templates used 7.5% payroll taxes with no workers' compensation, staffed a 1-person 'with overnight supervision' arrangement at 82 hours/week, and assumed full payment from month 1. DDA warns payment can take up to 180 days [S14], and employer FICA alone is 7.65% [S42].
The old materials predate the October 6, 2025 waiver consolidation (Family Supports and Community Supports merged into Community Pathways) [S1] and the pending FY2027 2% rate reduction [S5][S6].
